sentences.text: The name Cathayopterus means "China wing," derived from the historical name Cathay for China. The only known fossil is a skull showing teeth that splay outwards at the tip of the snout.
The known skull fossil is incomplete and damaged on the left side.
Its teeth splay outwards at the tip of the snout, a unique adaptation for its feeding style.
This creature lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
The genus Cathayopterus was described in 2006 by Wang Xiaolin and Zhou Zhonghe.
Cathayopterus was likely a filter feeder, consuming small invertebrates from the water, feeding by filtration like Ctenochasma and Pterodaustro.
Cathayopterus likely roamed around waterways to feed.
Cathayopterus is classified within the suborder Pterodactyloidea and in the family Ctenochasmatidae.
Phylogenetic analysis places Cathayopterus as a basal member of the family Ctenochasmatidae, a placement confirmed by a cladistic analysis by Lü Junchang in 2007.
Cathayopterus lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
